tool.name: session_entropy_check
tool.description:
Analyze session-cookie predictability / entropy. Two acquisition modes:
**1. auth-N-times** — provide `target_url` and `cookie_name`. Tool hits the URL `samples` times via cluster-A and reads the named cookie from each `Set-Cookie` response.
**2. pre-collected** — provide `cookie_values: list[str]` directly. Useful when the agent / wrapper has already harvested cookies via its own login flow.
Analyses applied to the sample set:
- **Sample diversity** — `unique_count < 2` → critical CWE-330 (cookie is constant across logins). - **Shannon entropy** (per-cookie average + min, in bits) — < 32 bits → high; 32-64 bits → medium; 64-80 bits → low; ≥ 80 bits → no entropy finding. - **Alphabet detection** — auto-detects hex_lower / hex_upper / base64_urlsafe / base64_standard / base32 / printable. Used for χ² bias. - **Pearson χ²** vs uniform distribution over the detected alphabet. p < 0.001 → bias finding (medium). - **Sequential-counter detection** — strips common prefix/suffix from cookie values; if the residue decodes to a monotonically-increasing decimal or hex sequence → high CWE-330 (sessions are predictable from a single observed cookie). - **NIST SP 800-22 mini-tests** on the concatenated bit stream: - Frequency / monobit - Runs test - Longest-run test (M=8 block) Each failure → medium CWE-330 (only when entropy ≥ 64 bits; otherwise the entropy finding subsumes the NIST/χ² finding).
Severity: - **Critical** CWE-330 — cookie is constant across logins. - **High** CWE-330 — sequential-counter detected; or avg Shannon entropy < 32 bits. - **Medium** CWE-330 — entropy 32-64 bits; or any NIST sub-test fails (when entropy ≥ 64); or χ² p < 0.001. - **Low** CWE-330 — entropy 64-80 bits.
Skip / soft-fail: - `samples < 2` collected (and no `cookie_values`) → tool returns `inconclusive=True` (the endpoint may not mint a fresh cookie per request). - `--exclude-path` blocks the URL → graceful no-op. - `cookie_values` < 2 → inconclusive.
**Safety**: - Read-only. - Default `samples=16`, max 128. Per-probe rate-limit comes from cluster-A `--rate-limit`. - Composes with cluster-A safety (`--exclude-path` / `--rate-limit` / `--auth-*`). - All findings carry severity-tailored `description_plain` + `recommended_action` (use a CSPRNG — `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` in Python, `crypto/rand` in Go, `SecureRandom` in Java; minimum 128 bits of entropy; rotate on privilege escalation; never derive session IDs from user IDs / timestamps / sequential counters) and `verification_status=needs_review` since low-sample-size analyses have variance — the agent should re-run with `samples=64` if flagged and the user wants confirmation.

parameter.name: target_url
parameter.description: URL that mints the session cookie. Required unless `cookie_values` is supplied. Bare hostnames are auto-prefixed with `https://`. Examples: `https://app.example.com/login`, `https://api.example.com/auth/init`.

parameter.name: cookie_name
parameter.description: Name of the cookie to harvest from `Set-Cookie`. Default `session`. Common alternatives: `JSESSIONID`, `PHPSESSID`, `connect.sid`, `_app_session`, `sid`.

parameter.name: samples
parameter.description: How many cookies to harvest in auth-N-times mode. Default 16, min 2, max 128.

parameter.name: method
parameter.description: HTTP method for the auth probe. Default `GET`. Use `POST` for form-based login endpoints.

parameter.name: body
parameter.description: Optional request body (e.g. `username=test&password=test` for POST-form logins).

parameter.name: headers
parameter.description: Optional extra request headers (e.g. `{"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"}`). Cluster-A `--auth-*` env headers are layered on top automatically.

parameter.name: cookie_values
parameter.description: Pre-harvested cookie values. When supplied, bypasses the HTTP probe phase entirely. Useful when the agent / wrapper has already collected cookies via its own login flow.

returns.description:
{success, target_url?, cookie_name, samples_requested, samples_collected, unique_count, analyses: {samples, unique_count, shannon_entropy_avg_bits, shannon_entropy_min_bits, alphabet, chi_squared, chi_squared_p_value, sequential_counter: {detected, evidence}, nist: {frequency: {passed, proportion}, runs: {passed, run_count}, longest_run: {passed, longest_run}}}, findings_emitted, inconclusive?, reason?}.
The agent should follow up high-severity findings by re-running with `samples=64` to rule out small-sample variance, then attempt session prediction (extrapolate from observed values to predict the next minted session ID and verify with a fresh login).
